title: Collections Reference — Delinquency, Reinstatement and Write-Off on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Collections Reference — Delinquency, Reinstatement and Write-Off on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

The delinquency threshold, the write-off threshold, the reinstatement limit, the repricing trigger and the repricing review window on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan are the figures the hardship and delinquency training note and the rates disclosure state for the plan's promotional term.

**Falling delinquent.** A plan whose oldest unpaid scheduled payment reaches the term's delinquency threshold in calendar days is marked past due, and it stays past due until the arrears are cleared.

**Being brought current.** A plan is brought current and reinstated only while it stands past due, and it returns to active once the arrears are cleared.

**The reinstatement limit.** A plan is reinstated only when the number of days past due carried at the time of the request has not exceeded the reinstatement limit for its term, counted from the earliest payment due date printed on a statement that is still unpaid. Days past due are counted in whole calendar days from the earliest unpaid payment due date to the handling date, weekends and store holidays included, and part days are never rounded up.

**Write-off.** A plan that reaches the term's write-off threshold in days past due is written off to collections, the balance standing at the moment of write-off is recorded, and the plan closes.

**Repricing.** A plan repriced to the penalty rate because it missed the term's trigger number of scheduled payments inside the repricing review window keeps that rate until the review passes clean.

**After write-off.** Once a plan is written off the desk no longer services it and the customer is directed to the collections partner; reinstating a written-off plan is not something this desk can do.

## Days past due at the boundary (hypothetical dates)

The earliest unpaid payment due date printed on a statement is 1 April, on a term whose reinstatement limit is 90 days and whose write-off threshold is 180 days. Counting whole calendar days from 1 April, weekends and store holidays included:

| Handling date | Days past due | Reinstatement |
|---|---|---|
| 29 June | 89 | Within the limit |
| 30 June | 90 | Within the limit: the limit is not exceeded at the limit itself |
| 1 July | 91 | The limit is exceeded; the plan is not reinstated |

On the same plan, 180 days past due is the point at which the plan is written off to collections and closes.
